column49: Predict statistical superiority to placebo on the Week 16 ACR50 endpoint. | ARGO's induction groups achieved statistically significant placebo-adjusted ACR50 differences (60 mg: P=0.012; 120 mg: P=0.009), whereas the non-induction 60 mg arm did not (P=0.086). Phase 2 groups were small and only about 17% had previous biologic exposure; the outcome of IZAR-2 remains unknown.
column54: Predict a manageable safety profile without a new trial-threatening signal. | The 207-patient ARGO Phase 2 trial reported sonelokimab was generally well tolerated, with nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infections, injection-site erythema, and headache among common events; four mild-to-moderate oral candidiasis cases were observed. The separate IZAR-1 Phase 3 blinded safety analysis (August 2026) reported no new safety signals. IZAR-2 studies anti-TNF inadequate responders; its actual safety results are still unavailable.
column59: The mechanism is biologically credible for psoriatic arthritis. | PsA involves IL-17A/F-driven inflammation; the established dual-IL-17 inhibitor class and sonelokimab's ARGO joint/skin responses support this pathway. Mechanistic plausibility alone does not establish IZAR-2 efficacy.

column104: Multidomain disease control is more likely than not. | ARGO reported MDA improvements and IZAR-1 disclosed a 41.2% MDA rate at Week 16 in the treated bio-naive cohort. MDA is harder to achieve than symptom-only responses, especially in resistant disease.
column109: Functional improvement is anticipated, though strength of separation is uncertain. | ARGO showed improving HAQ-DI over 24 weeks, although its Week 12 placebo comparison was not statistically significant. IZAR-1 later disclosed meaningful HAQ-DI improvement in biologic-naive patients.
column114: Physical quality-of-life gains are plausible. | IZAR-1 reported an improvement of 6.54 points in SF-36 physical component for the treated group; ARGO showed broader patient-reported benefits. No corresponding IZAR-2 comparison is available.
column119: Pain relief is expected to accompany joint improvement. | ARGO found nominally significant improvements versus placebo in patient arthritis pain assessments and global disease activity. TNF-IR patients may experience a smaller or more variable benefit.

column134: Biological activity is plausible, but convincing subgroup evidence is lacking. | ARGO observed numerical improvements but could not show statistically significant effects in these domains because few participants had them at baseline. IZAR-2 could improve precision, but subgroup results are unknown.
column139: Evidence is insufficient to forecast a definitive axial benefit. | ARGO observed some BASDAI symptom reductions but did not clinically classify axial PsA or establish consistent placebo-adjusted axial efficacy. IZAR-2 is not an axial-specific confirmatory trial.
column144: Sustained efficacy is plausible but far from proven. | ARGO ACR50 and skin outcomes generally persisted or improved to Week 24. Both IZAR studies follow patients through Week 52, but longer-term IZAR-2 durability is unreported and discontinuations could alter it.
column149: Expected class-related infections should usually be manageable. | ARGO reported relatively low rates of nasopharyngitis, URTI, and four mild-to-moderate oral candidiasis cases. A larger, treatment-experienced Phase 3 cohort may reveal different frequencies.
column154: A trial-threatening new signal is not the leading expectation, but rare risks remain. | ARGO had no observed IBD or major adverse cardiovascular events in its small sample; IZAR-1's disclosed blinded safety analysis reported no new signals. Neither excludes rare or longer-term events in IZAR-2.
column159: Retention is likely to support the planned primary analysis. | Most ARGO participants completed treatment and its early discontinuation was below 3%; MoonLake described low IZAR-1 Week 16 dropout. IZAR-2 follow-up and anti-TNF intolerance may introduce more missingness.

Registered population and eligibility: Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of IPF as determined by the Investigator based on American Thoracic Society (ATS)/European Respiratory Society (ERS)/Japanese Respiratory Society (JRS)/Latin American Thoracic Society (ALAT) clinical practice guidelines.
* Chronic cough for ≥8 weeks prior to Screening.
* PGI-Severity Score ≥ 2 at Screening.
* Forced vital capacity (FVC) ≥40 percent (%) of predicted at Screening.
* Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide (DLCO) ≥25% of predicted during Screening or within 12 weeks prior to Screening.
* Participants who are currently taking antifibrotic medication (nintedanib, pirfenidone, nerandomilast) approved for IPF should be on a stable dose for at least 6 weeks prior to the Baseline Visit.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Clinical diagnosis or clinical suspicion of an upper or lower respiratory tract infection in the last 8 weeks prior to the Screening visit or during Screening.
* Hospitalization for any respiratory illness (including acute exacerbation of IPF) within 2 months prior to Screening.

Note: Other protocol-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply.. Eligibility criteria alone do not establish external generalizability.
